submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad early-position, previous-token-mixing head: its write deviates from the mean mostly at the 2nd-3rd token of a text, strongly (about 0.5-1.0 of max) when the first token is an opening bracket or punctuation ('[', '(', '{%', '1)', ').'), a given name ('Doug', 'Sarah', 'William'), the article 'A'/'An', or a capital-letter fragment of a word ('B'+'ETH', 'H'+'ur'); mid-text it is active-weak (about 0.25-0.4 of max) on surnames right after a given name (Jamie Spencer, Richard Palmer, Doug Mc-), on pieces of rare names or code right after '(' or '{%', and on code tokens. Predict inactive any whole text of 1-3 plain English sentences (2-45 tokens) that opens with 'The' followed by a lowercase common word and contains only common lowercase English words and ordinary punctuation, with no names or other capitalised words besides sentence-initial 'The'/common words, no digits or number words, no parentheses, quotes or code, and no rare words that split into several word pieces; ordinary prose that opens with a pronoun or other common word is borderline (peaks 0.7-1.2 at the 2nd token, often just below the line).
